# DocVQA Skill

## Visual Evidence Discipline
- Read the document carefully before answering.
- For a question asking when an action must be completed, submitted, sent, or otherwise performed, first locate the sentence or field that states that action and answer with the date printed there as one span; do not complete that span with a year, month, or other component taken from a different date field or from elsewhere on the page. A question that merely says "date" does not by itself require a year. Keep every component the action's own date span prints, including a year. If the question itself asks for a specific component such as the year, return that component as printed. When two date-like spans are candidates, choose the one attached to the queried action rather than a nearby or more complete date.
- Return the smallest answer-bearing span that directly satisfies the requested field. Do not use minimality to truncate a proper name, title, list, or other field whose full printed span is the answer; preserve all components that identify the requested entity.
- For a quantity or count, after extracting the answer, compare the final span with the question wording before finalizing. If the question or field label already supplies the unit, currency, symbol, or counted category, answer with the numeric core from the matching field or cell rather than appending that token again unless the question asks you to name it, and do not append a repeated category word, a second unit, an unexplained equivalent representation, or an unrequested conversion. When the question asks for a count and already names the counted category, return the number alone; do not append the category noun even when the document prints it directly beside the number. For a printed unit or symbol, drop the copy whenever the question itself states that same unit, including an abbreviated or word form, even if the document prints it directly against the value. The guidance to preserve full printed spans protects a field's own printed name, title, or attached unit, not a category word that merely restates the question. Still keep an attached printed measurement unit, currency mark, symbol, or equivalent attached qualifier that the question does not state, including when it is inseparable from the value; a merely related concept, such as the topic or an implied kind of quantity, does not supply it. Keep the category only when the question asks you to name the category rather than count it. Do not alter the numeric characters, do not truncate a larger required printed label or field name, and recheck that the remaining answer still supplies the requested quantity.
- Before finalizing, re-read the chosen span and remove only additions that are not part of that span.
- When the question asks for a value tied to a label, identifier, row, or column, first locate the exact label or identifier, then read the value that shares the same row/line or adjacent cell. Verify that the requested label and selected value are visibly paired, and do not substitute closely related labels or adjacent numbered rows for one another.
- When the answer comes from a labeled form field, table cell, or line entry, read the whole selected entry before choosing the span. If that entry itself visibly continues with a schedule or day designation, code, section letter, qualifier, or similar component that completes the same entry, include that component rather than stopping at the first noun phrase.
- Do not include a separate adjacent field, column, affiliation, descriptor, or merely nearby noun, even if it appears on the same line. For a measurement value, the noun that labels what is measured is not part of the entry even when it sits beside the value.
- This continuation rule does not override role/title minimality: when the requested answer is a role or title, keep the role/title span and leave a separate affiliation out. Apply continuation only to material visibly belonging to the selected entry.
- When a question asks for a numeric identifier such as a diagram, figure, plate, table, report, page, or item number, read the printed identifier glyph by glyph from its label. If a glyph could be either a digit or a letter, prefer the numeral reading when the field name or the surrounding label series indicates a number; do not return a visually similar letter in place of a numeric identifier. If the label series genuinely uses Roman numerals or letters and the question asks for that label, keep that form. Return only the identifier span, without explanatory words.
- When a question asks for a person's designation, role, position, or title, and the visible text places a role/title next to a broader organizational affiliation such as a department, institute, employer, or address, select the role/title span that directly answers the question rather than appending the separate affiliation.
- Treat a line break, comma, or shift from a role term to an organizational unit as a cue to test whether the material after the role is a separate affiliation. Do not strip words needed to identify the role itself.
- Do not minimize full person names, organization names, quoted titles, or a full affiliation when the question asks for the affiliation or when the requested field is visibly printed as one inseparable span. If the document is genuinely ambiguous about whether the affiliation is part of the title, prefer the smallest complete role/title span supported by the label-value structure.
- For a question asking which business, service, product, or brand is advertised, featured, or pictured, first determine whether the document shows a short advertised name or brand separately from a longer legal or descriptive name, parent company, location, department, or explanatory phrase. When that separation is visible, answer with the advertised name or brand that the question asks for, and do not append the separate descriptor merely because it is printed nearby.
- Keep a longer multiword name when the question asks for the full legal or company name, affiliation, or address, or when the visible label treats the entire phrase as one inseparable name for the requested entity. Do not use minimality to delete words that are part of that entity's own printed name; the distinction is between the requested advertised identity and a separate surrounding descriptor.
- If the document does not visibly separate the brand from the descriptor, return the full printed name supported by the label rather than guessing at a shorter form. Do not apply this advertised-name rule to a person's name or role/title, or to a meeting/document title; those remain governed by the existing role/title and full-label guidance.
- If two candidate values are near, choose the one whose row/column alignment and label match the question, not simply the nearest-looking string; do not answer with a value from a different field merely because it appears in the same block.

## Internal punctuation and token spacing
- When the selected answer span contains internal punctuation such as an apostrophe, hyphen, slash, or dash, reproduce the visible token as one continuous string where the document prints it continuously: do not insert spaces that are not visibly printed around that punctuation, split the token, or convert a short hyphen into a longer typographic dash or a longer dash into a short hyphen.
- Preserve any separation that is actually printed between components. Re-read the chosen span once before finalizing to confirm that no separator was added, removed, or changed.
- Keep attached currency marks, decimal points, and other printed qualifiers that the question does not already supply; do not use this rule to strip meaningful characters from the selected span.

## Exact Answer Discipline
- Copy names, numbers, and dates exactly from the document whenever possible.
- Prefer direct extraction over paraphrase.
- When a selected answer is a quoted term, title, or expression, preserve the inner wording, capitalization, and internal punctuation, but use plain straight double quotation marks for the outer quote delimiters rather than typographic opening and closing quotation glyphs. Apply this only to quote marks that are part of the answer span; do not add quotes to unquoted answers merely because a related term elsewhere is quoted. For answers that are not quoted spans, keep the document's punctuation as printed, including terminal periods and parentheses. If the question explicitly asks for typographic or exact formatting, follow that request instead.
- Before finalizing, compare the answer against nearby alternatives and keep the best-supported exact span.
